I implemented `tokenize`, `lookup`, `isTruthy`, and `render`. All 10 tests pass with `npm test`.

- **`src/lexer.ts`**: splits the template into text and tag tokens. It handles `{{ }}` and `{{{ }}}`, trims tag contents, and throws `unterminated tag` when a tag is never closed.
- **`src/lookup.ts`**: `lookup` walks dotted paths through own properties of objects and arrays only. Strings are never descended into, so `name.length` and `name.0` are missing. `isTruthy` follows JavaScript, except empty arrays are false.
- **`src/render.ts`**: parses tokens into a tree of text, value, and `if`/`else` nodes, then evaluates it. Filters (`upper`, `lower`, `default: x`) run left to right. Unknown filters and misplaced `else`/`/if` tags throw the messages from the README. Values are HTML-escaped with the existing `escapeHtml` unless triple braces are used.

I also checked a few README edge cases by hand: `{{ constructor }}` renders empty, `name.length` is missing, a lone `}}` is copied as text, and a second `else` throws `unexpected {{else}}`.

I couldn't run `tsc` because `npx` could not fetch it from the registry (403), so the type-check is unverified. The code was written to the strict settings in `tsconfig.json`.
